title: Alliances listing copy + infra readiness checklist (AWS & Azure)
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a combined marketing copy + technical readiness checklist intended for the Alliances and GTM teams to use when preparing Redwood Inference listings for cloud marketplaces (AWS Marketplace and Azure Marketplace). It’s a working draft: marketing copy variants for listings, technical items required by each marketplace, asset list, and a short onboarding runbook for partner engineering.

Status / context:
- Drafted for the Alliances sync 2024-09-12.
- Goal: produce marketplace-ready artifacts (short + long copy, required legal commercial items, and a verified infra checklist) that engineering can validate.
- Primary marketplaces targeted: AWS (SaaS & AMI + container options) and Azure (SaaS + Azure Marketplace SaaS offer).

Listing copy: short headline variations (30–60 chars)
- "Predictable LLM inference, production-ready"
- "Low-latency LLM serving across clouds"
- "Redwood Inference — economical, reliable LLM serving"

One-line summary (for catalog listing metadata)
- "High-performance LLM inference platform with unified API, dedicated capacity, and private deployment options for secure, low-cost production usage."

3-sentence description (for expanded listing)
- "Redwood Inference delivers predictable, low-latency LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Ship features faster with an API that supports streaming, function/tool calling, and model rollouts, while optimizing cost with intelligent batching, caching, and quantization profiles. Built for engineering teams—includes observability, SLA-backed dedicated capacity, and private deployment with KMS integrations for regulated workloads."

Feature bullets (for marketplace highlights)
- "Unified API: same interface across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- "Predictable economics: dedicated GPU pools, autoscaling, and cost-optimization tooling."
- "Production observability: per-route latency/cost breakdowns, tracing, and eval-driven quality alerts."
- "Secure deployments: VPC/on-prem options, KMS/HSM key management, SOC2-ready controls."

Pricing blurb (short)
- "Usage-based pricing for hosted usage; reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated; enterprise licensing for Private deployments. Contact sales for private offers and marketplace pricing options."

Call-to-action variations
- "Start with free credits — see performance benchmarks in the listing."
- "Request a demo or private offer for dedicated capacity and SLAs."

Assets required for listing (marketing)
- High-res logo (PNG + SVG) — light and dark background variants.
- 2–3 product screenshots (Console: model selection, routing, cost breakdown).
- 1 short demo GIF (generation streaming).
- One-pager PDF: features + compliance summary.
- One-line SEO keywords: LLM inference, model serving, low-latency inference, dedicated GPU, private deployment.

Marketplace-specific technical & commercial checklist (working):
Common items (both AWS & Azure):
- Seller/partner account setup (account ID, marketplace registration) — confirm account in partner console.
- Contact info for technical & commercial leads (name, email, phone).
- SOC2 audit report or statement of compliance (or plan + timeline).
- Support SLA matrix and contact method (email + portal).
- Partner MOU or marketplace private offer terms (if applicable).

AWS Marketplace (SaaS / AMI / Container) checklist:
- Listing type confirmed: SaaS (preferred) OR AMI/container. Decide based on customer preference for private deployments.
- SaaS integration: implement AWS Metering Service (if using metered billing) OR provide private offer pricing flow.
- Authentication: support for AWS Marketplace entitlement check (token exchange) and SAML/OAuth for customer identity if required.
- Networking: document IP allowlists, recommended VPC peering steps, and port requirements for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Image artifacts: container image in ECR or AMI, with stable tag and vulnerability scan report.
- Health checks: a lightweight /health endpoint returning 200 and version metadata.
- Telemetry: CloudWatch metrics integration or instructions for pushing telemetry; list of required metrics for marketplace listing (uptime, error-rate).
- Billing metadata: SKU mapping, unit of measure, and price dimension details.
- Security: KMS integration guidance for customers; documented data-at-rest and in-transit encryption.

Azure Marketplace checklist (SaaS offers):
- Listing type: SaaS offer registration in Partner Center. Confirm lead disposition behavior and metering approach.
- Authentication: support for Azure AD SSO integration and mention of required app registration steps.
- Container image: container registry (ACR) guidance for private deployment flows.
- Managed identities: document how customers can use managed identities with Redwood integrations.
- Monitoring: support for Application Insights or guidance for forwarding logs/metrics.
- Legal/commercial: fill in marketplace commerce terms and provide contact for private offers/managed services.

Private/Dedicated deployment notes (common asks from marketplace customers):
- VPC peering or private link approach for hosting in customer accounts.
- KMS/HSM key handling: recommended flow and PR templates for key exchange.
- Data retention & purge policy (default retention windows, logs retention).
- Baseline performance matrix: tokens/sec by model class and GPU type; include sample benchmark artifacts.

Engineering runbook (minimal steps to validate a listing):
1) Confirm seller account and permissions with marketplace team.
2) Produce marketing assets + copy variants; copy sign-off by marketing.
3) Produce and upload container images / AMI with tags -> run vulnerability scan.
4) Implement and test health endpoints and metrics push.
5) Validate entitlement/marketplace token flow (AWS/Azure sandbox).
6) Smoke test: onboarding flow + sample inference request (measure p95 latency, error rate).
7) Fill legal/commercial fields and attach SOC2/other compliance artifacts.
8) Submit listing draft to marketplace; track review items and address feedback.

Open questions / decisions to resolve (TODOs)
- Which listing type do we prioritize for Q4 launch (SaaS preferred; but some large prospects prefer AMI)? Decision owner: Alliances (Sabrina).
- Metering vs private offer: default to private offer for enterprise deals — verify engineering support for both. Owner: Sales Ops (Ethan).
- Benchmark artifacts: do we publish model-level tokens/sec for public listing or keep only representative numbers? Owner: Applied ML (Noah) — due 2024-09-20.

Short engineer checklist for preflight (copy to engineering tickets)
- [ ] Provide image/AMI details and registry/URI.
- [ ] Add /health endpoint and expose version header.
- [ ] Add lightweight metrics (uptime, avg-latency, error-rate).
- [ ] Confirm telemetry integration (CloudWatch / AppInsights).
- [ ] Validate entitlement token exchange in marketplace sandbox.

Approval and sign-offs required
- Marketing: final copy + assets (Maya).
- Legal: marketplace terms review (Legal lead).
- Security & Compliance: SOC2 / encryption docs (Security).
- Product: feature and pricing accuracy (Product).

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep copy short and engineer-friendly — marketplaces are often scanned quickly.
- Include demo link and quickstart snippet in the listing if allowed.
- Keep commercial fields flexible: prefer private offers for large customers; metered for self-serve.

Next steps (immediate)
- Sync with Applied ML for benchmark artifact decision (Noah) — schedule 30-min sync 2024-09-15.
- Attach required logos + screenshots to this doc (Maya to collect).
- Create engineering ticket for entitlement integration test (Ethan).

Revision history:
- 2024-08-09: initial draft (Maya).
- 2024-09-02: added Azure marketplace checklist (Sabrina).
- 2024-09-12: updated open questions and moved to in_review.
